players.product: on-premises superconducting quantum computers (five-qubit IQM Spark; IQM Radiance, approximately 20 to 150 qubits) and IQM Resonance cloud

quarterly_data.signal: IQM prospectus, orders and revenue mix (EUR): 2025 order intake was 68,522 thousand (2024: 35,150 thousand), taking order backlog from 30,132 thousand to 67,321 thousand at year-end; of the transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations, 32,987 thousand is expected within one year and 34,334 thousand later. Revenue from on-premises quantum computer systems rose 104% to 30.6 million in 2025, cloud-based usage revenue to 0.3 million and co-development revenue fell to 0.3 million; revenue recognized over time was about 56% (2024: 92%). Q2 2026 order intake was 10,332 thousand (hardware and service 9,871 thousand), against 6,144 thousand a year earlier. Sales to the public sector - universities, national research institutions and other public sources including the EU's EuroHPC Joint Undertaking funding program - were 98.0% of first-half 2026 revenue (99.5% a year earlier).
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 order intake EUR 68,522 thousand; public sector 98.0% of H1 2026 revenue; Q2 2026 order intake EUR 10,332 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: IQM prospectus, supply and capex: in the first half of 2026 IQM made EUR 8,466 thousand of advance payments to vendors for raw materials, components and other production-related goods for future delivery; on June 9, 2026 it settled the termination of a supply agreement for an automated testing system under development (equipment to characterize and validate quantum chips before deployment), receiving a EUR 1,000 thousand refund. Purchases of property, plant and equipment were EUR 11,536 thousand in 2025 and EUR 7,159 thousand in the first half of 2026; cash was EUR 113.4 million at June 30, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: vendor advance payments EUR 8,466 thousand (H1 2026); 2025 capex EUR 11,536 thousand
